''' Archibald "Archie" Howie''' (born 8 March 1934)<ref name="whoswho"/> is a British [[physicist]] and emeritus professor at the University of Cambridge, known for his pioneering work on the interpretation of [[transmission electron microscopy|transmission electron microscope]] images of crystals. Born in 1934, he attended [[Kirkcaldy High School]] and the [[University of Edinburgh]]. He received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]]<ref>{{cite book |last1=Howie |first1=A. |title=Electron microscope transmission studies of single metal crystals |date=1961 |publisher=University of Cambridge |url=https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?did=4&uin=uk.bl.ethos.604672}}</ref> from the [[University of Cambridge]], where he subsequently took up a permanent post. He has been a fellow of [[Churchill College, Cambridge|Churchill College]] since its foundation, and was President of its [[Common Room (university)|Senior Combination Room]] (SCR) until 2010.

In 1965, with [[Peter Hirsch (metallurgist)|Hirsch]], [[M.J. Whelan|Whelan]], Pashley and Nicholson, he published the seminal text ''Electron Microscopy of Thin Crystals''.<ref>[[Peter Hirsch (metallurgist)|P. Hirsch]], '''A. Howie''', R. Nicholson, D. W. Pashley and [[M.J. Whelan|M. J. Whelan]] (1965/1977) Electron microscopy of thin crystals (Butterworths/Krieger, London/Malabar FL) {{ISBN|0-88275-376-2}}</ref> He was elected to the [[Royal Society]] in 1978 and awarded their [[Royal Medal]] in 1999. In 1992 he was awarded the [[Guthrie Medal and Prize]]. He was elected an Honorary Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] in 1995.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.rse.org.uk/fellow/archibald-howie/|title=Professor Archibald Howie CBE FRS HonFRSE - The Royal Society of Edinburgh|work=The Royal Society of Edinburgh|access-date=2018-02-12|language=en-GB}}</ref> He was head of the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] from 1989 to 1997.
